findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the `git archive` promisor batch-fetch claim with a citable source (git release note, `builtin/archive.c` source analysis, or documented `unpack-trees` usage by git archive) before treating the snapshot.py exclusion as settled; if the claim cannot be verified, file a follow-up analogous to 983f rather than asserting 'no change required'.
evidence: Plan states: 'GIT_TRACE2_EVENT child_start counting shows 40 missing blobs resolved by exactly ONE batched child git fetch ... git archive therefore DOES batch its promisor prefetch'

Official git partial-clone docs: 'Dynamic object fetching tends to be slow as objects are fetched one at a time. checkout (and any other command using unpack-trees) has been taught to bulk pre-fetch all required missing blobs in a single batch.' — git archive is NOT in the named set.

The fallback mechanism described in git docs is: 'When the normal object lookup fails to find an object, Git invokes promisor_remote_get_direct() to try to get the object from a promisor remote' — this is the per-object dynamic fetch path, not a batch path.
The plan does not cite a git release note, commit, or documentation source confirming that git archive specifically was updated to use the batch pre-fetch path.
findings.finding: The plan's justification for excluding `src/rebar/llm/workflow/snapshot.py` from scope rests on an unverified capability assertion: that `git archive` on a blobless partial clone issues exactly ONE batched child `git fetch` for all missing blobs. Official git partial-clone documentation (git-scm.com/docs/partial-clone) explicitly states that the bulk pre-fetch optimization applies only to 'checkout (and any other command using unpack-trees)' — git archive does NOT use unpack-trees, and there is no documented evidence it performs batched lazy-fetch for missing blobs. If the assertion is wrong, the `git archive` call in snapshot.py would exhibit the same sequential-per-object fetch pattern as the read-tree/checkout-index pair fixed by 747f, but that site would be left unbounded and out of scope.
findings.location: Plan section 'Resolved: the `git archive` question (was flagged UNJUDGED)'
scenarios: If git archive on a blobless clone faults in blobs one-at-a-time via the dynamic fetch fallback (the default non-unpack-trees path), snapshot.py has the same 747f bug class and is incorrectly excluded from scope.
The error is compounded because snapshot.py is owned by a parallel session, so the exclusion may persist even after the parallel session closes.
findings.suggested_fix: Search the git changelog or builtin/archive.c source for evidence that git archive calls prefetch_object_list() or the equivalent batch-prefetch path. If no such evidence exists, the 'measured read-only' claim should be downgraded to 'inconclusive' and a follow-up ticket filed (analogous to 983f) rather than asserting the exclusion is settled.
